headline: Adapting cancer omics models across cohorts, cell lines and tumour types
label: Transfer Learning In Cancer Omics
summary: Recent preprints test whether transfer and domain adaptation keep cancer omics models accurate beyond their training cohorts.
synthesis: The dominant thread is transferring learned relationships across data regimes: from older to younger breast cancer cohorts via layer-specific transfer elastic net, from cell-line pharmacogenomics to TCGA tumours via MODAE+ domain adaptation, and across cancer types for axillary lymph node metastasis prediction. Two further items anchor models to clinical or pathway structure: CAISL for LUAD survival with sparse molecular risk correction, and an Elastic Net that infers Hallmark pathway dependency in HNSCC from GDSC cell lines, validated on TCGA-HNSC and GSE65858. Evaluation is the sharper point. A multimodal ER/PR/HER2 model achieved strong cross-cohort AUCs yet showed poor calibration and no gain over a 3-gene baseline, while logistic regression led the TCGA classification comparison. These are tabular, transcriptomic and deep-learning adaptations rather than sequence-to-function models.
